analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram depicts SundaySky's Rendering as a Service (RAS) ecosystem on AWS. A user on a client device initiates a video rendering request through API Gateway, which forwards the request to the RAS Frontend Lambda function after performing throttling/validation using API keys and usage plans. The Lambda pushes job instructions into an SQS Jobs Queue, from which Rendering EC2 Instances (managed inside an Auto Scaling Group across multiple AZs using Spot instances) pull work. The EC2 instances send an immediate status response to an SQS Responses Queue, which the RAS Frontend Lambda polls to return a playlist file link back to the client device. Rendered video segments are stored in S3, from which CloudFront serves content to the client player. Two auxiliary automation loops are present: 1) Auto Scaling Loop: Step Functions triggers a Scaling Lambda every 15 seconds, which reads CloudWatch metrics emitted by the rendering EC2 instances and scales the Auto Scaling Group. 2) Interruption Handler Loop: CloudWatch Events captures Spot instance interruption warnings, triggering an Interruption Handler Lambda that calls an API on the target EC2 instance to drain rendering tasks and then detaches the instance from the Auto Scaling Group.
